Name: Accessibility
Definition: The degree to which the software is usable by people with disabilities, often through assistive technologies.

Name: Accountability
Definition: The degree to which the software keeps accurate records and has the ability to explain its operations.
Has positive effects on: Credibility; Integrity; Auditability; Traceability; Reliability; Correctness

Name: Accuracy
Definition: The capability of the software to retrieve and rank data accurately according to given specifications.

Name: Adaptability
Definition: The degree to which the software adapts its behavior based on information about its users and environment.

Name: Administrability
Definition: The extent to which users with elevated permissions can effectively configure the software.

Name: Affordability
Definition: The cost of the software as it relates to what the purchaser can afford.

Name: Atomicity
Definition: In databases, the assurance that transactions are treated as single units that either fully succeed or fail.

Name: Auditability
Definition: The degree to which the software logs actions and allows authorized inspection of these logs.

Name: Autonomy
Definition: The degree to which service-oriented software operates independently from its execution environment.

Name: Availability
Definition: The degree to which the software is ready and available for use.

Name: Capabilities
Definition: The range of actions, tasks, or functions that the software can perform.

Name: Compatibility
Definition: The degree to which the software can work effectively with other systems or software.

Name: Complexity
Definition: The degree of difficulty to understand, modify, or maintain the software.

Name: Composability
Definition: The degree to which the software's components can be assembled and reassembled.

Name: Confidentiality
Definition: The degree to which the software protects sensitive information from unauthorized access.

Name: Configurability
Definition: The extent to which settings and features within the software can be customized by the user.

Name: Consistency
Definition: The degree to which the software behaves and presents itself uniformly across different scenarios.

Name: Correctness
Definition: The extent to which the software performs its functions without error.

Name: Credibility
Definition: The degree to which the software is reliable and induces trust.

Name: Customizability
Definition: The degree to which the software allows the user to tailor features to their specific needs.

Name: Debuggability
Definition: The ease with which bugs can be discovered and fixed within the software.

Name: Degradability
Definition: The degree to which the software can gracefully reduce its functionality in the face of system constraints.

Name: Demonstrability
Definition: The ease with which the software's functions and capabilities can be demonstrated to others.

Name: Dependability
Definition: The extent to which the software can be relied upon to perform its functions accurately and consistently.

Name: Deployability
Definition: The degree to which the software can be easily installed, configured, and put into operation.

Name: Determinability
Definition: The extent to which the software's behavior can be predictably determined from its inputs and conditions.

Name: Discoverability
Definition: The degree to which the software's features and functionalities are easily discoverable by users.

Name: Distributability
Definition: The extent to which the software can be distributed across multiple platforms and environments.

Name: Durability
Definition: The degree to which the software can endure stress and continue to function over extended periods of time.

Name: Effectiveness
Definition: The ability of the software to achieve its goals and produce desired outcomes.

Name: Efficiency
Definition: The degree to which the software performs its functions without wasting resources.

Name: Evolvability
Definition: The extent to which the software can adapt to future changes in its environment or requirements.

Name: Extensibility
Definition: The degree to which new features or functionalities can be added to the existing software.

Name: Failure Transparency
Definition: The extent to which the software reveals or conceals its failures and the impact of those failures.

Name: Fault-Tolerance
Definition: The degree to which the software continues to function in the presence of errors or failures.

Name: Fidelity
Definition: The degree to which the software accurately represents or simulates real-world conditions or data.

Name: Flexibility
Definition: The ease with which the software can adapt to different tasks or scenarios.

Name: Functionality
Definition: The range and capabilities of tasks that the software can perform.

Name: Inspectability
Definition: The degree to which the software’s internal workings can be examined for debugging or analysis.

Name: Installability
Definition: The ease with which the software can be installed and set up for use.

Name: Integrity
Definition: The degree to which the software prevents unauthorized access and maintains the accuracy of data.

Name: Interchangeability
Definition: The ease with which components within the software can be exchanged.

Name: Interoperability
Definition: The degree to which the software can interact with other systems or software components.

Name: Learnability
Definition: The ease with which new users can understand and use the software.

Name: Localizability
Definition: The ability of the software to be adapted for different languages, regions, and cultures.

Name: Maintainability
Definition: The ease with which the software can be modified, updated, or corrected.

Name: Manageability
Definition: The extent to which the software can be efficiently managed and monitored.

Name: Mobility
Definition: The ability of the software to operate effectively on different devices or environments.

Name: Modifiability
Definition: The degree to which the software can be easily changed to add new features or fix issues.

Name: Modularity
Definition: The extent to which the software is composed of independent, interchangeable modules.

Name: Observability
Definition: The degree to which internal states of the software can be observed through outputs.

Name: Operability
Definition: The ease with which the software can be kept in a functioning state.

Name: Orthogonality
Definition: The independence between different features or components of the software.

Name: Performance
Definition: The effectiveness of the software in terms of speed, efficiency, and resource usage.

Name: Portability
Definition: The ease with which the software can be moved from one environment to another.

Name: Precision
Definition: The accuracy with which the software performs its calculations or processes.

Name: Predictability
Definition: The degree to which the software's behavior can be anticipated.

Name: Privacy
Definition: The degree to which the software ensures that unauthorized users cannot access, modify, or delete personal information.

Name: Producibility
Definition: The ease with which the software can be reliably reproduced or replicated.

Name: Provability
Definition: The extent to which formal methods can be used to prove the software's correctness.

Name: Recoverability
Definition: The ability of the software to restore its state and functionality after failure.

Name: Relevance
Definition: The degree to which the software meets the real-world needs of its users.

Name: Reliability
Definition: The ability of the software to function correctly and consistently.

Name: Repeatability
Definition: The degree to which the software provides the same output for the same input under the same conditions.

Name: Reproducibility
Definition: The ability to get the same results consistently across different environments and conditions.

Name: Resilience
Definition: The ability of the software to adapt and recover from adversity.

Name: Responsiveness
Definition: The software's ability to quickly respond to user input or system events.

Name: Reusability
Definition: The extent to which components of the software can be used in different contexts.

Name: Robustness
Definition: The ability of the software to cope with errors and unexpected conditions.

Name: Safety
Definition: The degree to which the software avoids causing harm to users or the environment.

Name: Scalability
Definition: The software's ability to handle increased loads efficiently.

Name: Seamlessness
Definition: The degree to which the software integrates its various components without visible gaps or inconsistencies.

Name: Securability
Definition: The ability of the software to protect against unauthorized access and data breaches.

Name: Self-Sustainability
Definition: The software's ability to maintain its operational state without external intervention.

Name: Serviceability/Supportability
Definition: The ease with which the software can be serviced, maintained, and supported.

Name: Simplicity
Definition: The degree to which the software is easy to understand and use.

Name: Stability
Definition: The extent to which the software remains reliable under different conditions.

Name: Standards Compliance
Definition: The degree to which the software adheres to industry or regulatory standards.

Name: Survivability
Definition: The ability of the software to endure and recover from catastrophic failures.

Name: Sustainability
Definition: The ability of the software to endure over time while meeting environmental and social requirements.

Name: Tailorability
Definition: The ease with which the software can be customized to meet specific user needs.

Name: Testability
Definition: The degree to which the software can be effectively tested to ensure it meets its requirements.

Name: Timeliness
Definition: The software's ability to perform tasks or provide responses within an acceptable time frame.

Name: Traceability
Definition: The ability to track changes, data flow, or user actions throughout the software.

Name: Transparency
Definition: The degree to which the software's actions and decision-making processes are visible to the user.

Name: Ubiquity
Definition: The extent to which the software is available and functional across various platforms and devices.

Name: Understandability
Definition: The ease with which users can comprehend the software's functions and use.

Name: Upgradability
Definition: The ease with which new features can be added or existing features can be modified.

Name: Usability
Definition: The degree to which the software is easy to use and provides a good user experience.

Name: Vulnerability
Definition: The extent to which the software is susceptible to unauthorized access or exploitation.
